https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1201

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/04a56d87a5016a2da486b6c19812782d5bbf562d
An IndirectContainer can be created using a server-managed predicate as the ldp:hasMemberRelation value.  This will generate potentially invalid triples.
For example, this gist demonstrates generating bogus fedora:lastModified triples with an IndirectContainer:
https://gist.github.com/escowles/29ab8f71ce39072ca12deb2ec11c4bd2

comments.body:
Esmé Cowles:  I'm taking a look at this issue.   Thanks for the clear illustration of the problem.  

How does the following proposed fix sound to you?

  1.  inspect the incoming puts for a ldp:hasMemberRelation value.
  2. if the value contains a server managed predicate, return a 400.

 

One question: is there a list of predicates that comprise the set of invalid values?  For example,  could assume that anything  defined in the FedoraTypes.java would be invalid? Or should I limit validate to fedora:* ? Your thoughts would be appreciated.
Danny Bernstein, that sounds good to me.  I think you can probably use the RdfLexicon.isManagedPredicate to check if the property is server-managed or not.

I suspect any of the managed-properties should not be allowed as the value of ldp:hasMemberRelation:

https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-api/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/api/RdfLexicon.java#L236-L245

...what Esmé Cowles said.
Andrew Woods, Esmé Cowles:  thanks - exactly what I was looking for.
